correctness.rationale: All positive starts become odd after at most three steps. For any odd n>=29, the composite, prime followed by composite, and twin-prime branches give a smaller odd state within 1, 2 or 3 steps, respectively; the strict decreasing stopping-time argument forces entry to the 13-state invariant graph. Euler prime-power bounds give phi(n)>=sqrt(n/2), so every inverse-totient solution phi(n)<=30 occurs at n<=1800. Full exact sieve enumeration yields the displayed inverse lists, which recursively close the two exceptional basins. All 24 exceptions are explicitly checked; the remaining basin is exhaustive. Finite testing of n<=100000 is supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial small odd shift is completely analyzed for every positive input. Besides coexistence of periods 1, 2 and 3, it proves that only 24 starts avoid the period-3 attractor, with a sharp universal threshold 67. These exact global basin sizes are mathematically informative and not consequences of the published eventual-periodicity and conditional period-size bounds.
